title: Imports and Setup
content: Imports SimpleGraph (undirected graphs), SimpleGraph.Coloring (graph colorability), Fintype (finite vertex sets), and general tactics. Opens the SimpleGraph namespace for concise notation.
mathContext: The formalization builds on Mathlib's `SimpleGraph` API, which models undirected graphs as symmetric irreflexive relations on a vertex type $V$. The `Colorable` predicate provides $\chi(G)$ via `SimpleGraph.Colorable k`.

title: Graph Orientation
content: An orientation assigns a direction to each edge: for every edge {u,v}, exactly one of (u->v) or (v->u) holds. Formalized as a structure with a directed relation `dir`, a coverage axiom, and a consistency axiom ensuring directed edges correspond to undirected edges.
mathContext: An **orientation** of $G$ is a digraph $D$ with $V(D) = V(G)$ where each edge $\{u,v\} \in E(G)$ becomes exactly one arc $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$. The structure captures the `covers` axiom ($G.\text{Adj}\, u\, v \Rightarrow \text{dir}\, u\, v \lor \text{dir}\, v\, u$) and `consistent` axiom ($\text{dir}\, u\, v \Rightarrow G.\text{Adj}\, u\, v$).

title: Acyclic Coloring
content: A coloring c : V -> Fin k is acyclic for orientation O if no directed edge connects two same-color vertices: O.dir u v implies c(u) != c(v). This is a simplification of the full condition (no monochromatic directed cycles), equivalent for finite graphs.
mathContext: An **acyclic coloring** of an oriented graph $(G, O)$ is a function $c : V \to [k]$ such that $c(u) \ne c(v)$ whenever $O.\text{dir}\, u\, v$. For finite graphs, this is equivalent to requiring no monochromatic directed cycle, since a monochromatic directed path of length $|V|$ must revisit a vertex.

title: HasAcyclicColoring
content: An orientation admits an acyclic k-coloring if there exists a function c : V -> Fin k satisfying the acyclicity condition. This is the existential wrapper used in defining the dichromatic number.
mathContext: The predicate `HasAcyclicColoring O k` asserts $\exists c : V \to [k],\, \text{IsAcyclicColoring}\, O\, c$. The dichromatic number minimizes $k$ over the universal quantifier on orientations.

title: Dichromatic Number
content: The dichromatic number delta(G) is defined as the infimum of {k : for all orientations O, there exists an acyclic k-coloring of O}. It measures the worst-case coloring complexity across all possible edge orientations.
mathContext: The **dichromatic number** $\delta(G) = \inf\{k \in \mathbb{N} : \forall O \in \text{Or}(G),\, \exists$ acyclic $k$-coloring of $O\}$. Introduced by Neumann-Lara (1982). For tournaments, $\delta(T)$ equals the minimum acyclic chromatic number. Always $\delta(G) \le \chi(G)$ since proper colorings are acyclic for any orientation.

title: Cochromatic Coloring
content: A cochromatic coloring partitions vertices so each color class is either a clique (all pairs adjacent) or an independent set (no pairs adjacent). This relaxes proper coloring by allowing monochromatic cliques.
mathContext: A **cochromatic coloring** is a partition $V = C_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup C_k$ where each $C_i$ induces either a complete graph or an empty graph. The **cochromatic number** $\zeta(G) = \min k$ over all such partitions. Since independent sets satisfy both conditions, $\zeta(G) \le \chi(G)$.

title: Cochromatic Number
content: The cochromatic number zeta(G) is the minimum k for which a cochromatic k-partition exists. Defined via sInf over the set of valid k values.
mathContext: The cochromatic number $\zeta(G) = \inf\{k : \exists c : V \to [k],\, \text{IsCochromatic}\, G\, c\}$. Introduced by Lesniak and Straight (1977). For perfect graphs, $\zeta(G) = \min(\chi(G), \theta(G))$ where $\theta$ is the clique cover number.

title: Dichromatic Number Bounded by Vertex Count
content: The dichromatic number is at most |V|. Any proper coloring (no adjacent vertices share a color) is automatically acyclic for every orientation, since monochromatic directed edges cannot exist.
mathContext: The axiom states $\delta(G) \le |V|$, a weaker form of $\delta(G) \le \chi(G) \le |V|$. The key insight: if $c$ is a proper $\chi(G)$-coloring, then for any orientation $O$, whenever $O.\text{dir}\, u\, v$ we have $G.\text{Adj}\, u\, v$ (by consistency), so $c(u) \ne c(v)$ (by properness). Hence $c$ is acyclic for $O$.

title: Cochromatic Number Bounded by Vertex Count
content: The cochromatic number is at most |V|. Any proper coloring gives a cochromatic partition since each independent color class is trivially cochromatic.
mathContext: States $\zeta(G) \le |V|$, a weakened form of $\zeta(G) \le \chi(G) \le |V|$. The bound $\zeta(G) \le \chi(G)$ is central to the implication Q2 $\Rightarrow$ Q1: if $\chi(G)$ is large then $\zeta(G)$ is large, so Q2 gives a subgraph with large $\delta$.

title: Bipartite Dichromatic Number
content: Bipartite graphs have dichromatic number at most 2. Any 2-coloring is proper, hence acyclic for all orientations. This is the single sorry in the file.
mathContext: If $G$ is 2-colorable (bipartite), then $\delta(G) \le 2$: the 2-coloring is proper, hence acyclic for every orientation. This shows the questions are interesting only for graphs with $\chi(G) \ge 3$. The proof requires showing the sInf is at most 2 given `G.Colorable 2`.

title: Question 1: Large Chi Forces Large Delta
content: Erdős and Neumann-Lara asked: for every k, does there exist f(k) such that chi(G) >= f(k) implies delta(G) >= k? Axiomatized as an open conjecture. This would establish that high chromatic number forces complex orientation-coloring structure.
mathContext: **Erdős-Neumann-Lara conjecture**: $\forall k,\, \exists f(k)$ such that $\chi(G) \ge f(k) \Rightarrow \delta(G) \ge k$. The formalization uses `G.Colorable f = false` as a proxy for $\chi(G) > f$. This is one of the central open problems connecting undirected and directed chromatic theory. A counterexample would require constructing graphs with unbounded $\chi$ but bounded $\delta$.

title: Question 2: Large Zeta Forces Subgraph with Large Delta
content: Erdős and Gimbel strengthened Question 1: does large cochromatic number force a subgraph with large dichromatic number? Since zeta(G) <= chi(G), a positive answer to Q2 implies Q1. Axiomatized as an open conjecture.
mathContext: **Erdős-Gimbel conjecture**: $\forall k,\, \exists g(k)$ such that $\zeta(G) \ge g(k) \Rightarrow \exists H \subseteq G$ with $\delta(H) \ge k$. This is strictly stronger than Q1 since $\zeta(G) \le \chi(G)$: large $\chi$ forces large $\zeta$, and Q2 then gives the subgraph with large $\delta$, and monotonicity gives $\delta(G) \ge \delta(H) \ge k$.

title: Complete Graph Dichromatic Number
content: For complete graphs K_n, the dichromatic number equals floor(n/2) + 1 (Neumann-Lara 1982). This shows delta can be much smaller than chi: delta(K_n) ~ n/2 while chi(K_n) = n.
mathContext: Neumann-Lara (1982) proved $\delta(K_n) = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$. Since $\chi(K_n) = n$, this gives the ratio $\delta(K_n)/\chi(K_n) \to 1/2$, showing dichromatic number can be roughly half the chromatic number. The proof uses the fact that any tournament on $n$ vertices can be acyclically colored with $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ colors.

title: Odd Cycle Dichromatic Number
content: For odd cycles C_{2k+1}, the dichromatic number is 2 while the chromatic number is 3. A simple example showing delta(G) < chi(G). Axiomatized as True due to missing cycle graph construction in Mathlib.
mathContext: For odd cycles $C_{2k+1}$: $\delta(C_{2k+1}) = 2$ while $\chi(C_{2k+1}) = 3$. Any orientation of $C_{2k+1}$ has at least one vertex whose two incident arcs go in opposite directions, allowing a 2-coloring. The axiom is stated as `True` since Mathlib lacks a cycle graph construction.

title: Subgraph Monotonicity
content: The dichromatic number is monotone under subgraphs: if H is a subgraph of G, then delta(H) <= delta(G). Any orientation of H extends to an orientation of G, so the maximum over orientations can only increase.
mathContext: **Subgraph monotonicity**: $H \subseteq G \Rightarrow \delta(H) \le \delta(G)$. This is crucial for the Q2 $\Rightarrow$ Q1 implication: Q2 gives $\exists H \subseteq G$ with $\delta(H) \ge k$, and monotonicity gives $\delta(G) \ge \delta(H) \ge k$. The proof: any $k$-coloring acyclic for all orientations of $G$ restricts to one acyclic for all orientations of $H$.

title: Existence of Acyclic Orientations
content: Acyclic orientations always exist (by induction on edges). For an acyclic orientation, any proper coloring is automatically acyclic, giving another proof that delta(G) <= chi(G).
mathContext: Every graph admits an acyclic orientation (order vertices and direct edges from smaller to larger). For such an orientation $O$, any proper $\chi(G)$-coloring is acyclic, giving $\delta(G) \le \chi(G)$. This structural result also connects to the theory of DAGs: an acyclic orientation makes the graph a DAG, and DAGs are always properly colorable by topological ordering.
